I've been working this land for 40 years. I know Quzhou's weather, the soil here, what the neighbors grow. I don't need to think too hard — I just do what has worked.

**Wheat (winter):** I plant wheat every October on my main 10 mu. I'll use the improved seed I buy from the township input shop — the same variety I've used for several years now. Good yield, doesn't fall over in wind. I'll rotary till before sowing, apply compound fertilizer as base, then topdress with urea at jointing. I irrigate three times: once before sowing to wet the bed, once at jointing, once at heading. Two rounds of pesticide — one herbicide early, one fungicide before heading. I expect around 450 jin per mu if the spring isn't too dry.

**Maize (summer):** Right after wheat harvest in June, I direct-seed maize into the stubble. No need to till — I've done no-till for maize the last few years, saves my back and the machine fee. Hybrid seed, same brand as last year. I apply fertilizer once at sowing and topdress at the big bell stage. Two irrigations if it's a dry summer, maybe just one if rain is enough. I'll spray once for stem borer. I expect 550 jin per mu.

**Stevia:** I have a contract with the stevia company, so I know they'll take the leaves. My 6.1 mu goes to stevia. I transplant in spring after the last frost, rotary till the plot beforehand. Stevia needs more water than wheat, so I irrigate five or six times through the season. I fertilize a bit lighter than grain crops — stevia doesn't need as much nitrogen or the leaves go bitter. Three pesticide rounds. I harvest the leaves twice in a season before frost kills the tops.

My wife helps with some of the hand work on the stevia. At 67, I can't do everything myself, so I hire the village machine for tillage and harvesting.
